headline: GLENCORE H1 PROFIT SURGES 86% TO $10.1B — Plans October ASX Secondary Listing; $1.5B Payout Declared As London Loses Mining Shine
snippet: Glencore reported an 86% surge in first-half 2026 adjusted EBITDA to US$10.1 billion and announced it will seek a secondary ASX listing via CHESS Depositary Interests in October 2026, targeting Australia's A$4.4 trillion superannuation pool and its resources-focused investor base — the latest blow to London's mining market, which has been losing primary listings to the ASX since BHP transferred in 2022. CEO Gary Nagle cited improved liquidity and a broader investor base as the rationale, alongside a US$1.5 billion shareholder distribution and full-year 2026 EBITDA guidance of approximately US$19.7 billion. For junior mining investors, the structural implication is directional: as the world's largest commodity trader tilts toward ASX-denominated capital, the pool of institutional investors exposed to copper, zinc, and coal developers on the ASX grows deeper and more competitive.

headline: REVIVAL GOLD DRILLS 131.7m @ 3.43 g/t AU AT JOSS ZONE — Including 42.5m @ 6.56 g/t And 11.58 g/t Spike; One Of Beartrack-Arnett's Strongest Intercepts Yet (TSX-V: RVG)
snippet: Revival Gold Inc. (TSX-V: RVG) released one of the strongest drill intercepts recorded at its Beartrack-Arnett Gold Project in Idaho: hole BT26-255D returned 131.7 metres at 3.43 g/t gold from 543 metres downhole at the Joss area, including 42.5 metres at 6.56 g/t and a high-grade spike of 12.1 metres at 11.58 g/t gold at depth — with true widths estimated at 40–50% of drilled width. The intercept confirms and extends high-grade underground sulphide mineralisation not drilled at Joss since 2022, within a 5,500-metre 2026 program explicitly targeting resource expansion for what could become Idaho's next standalone gold mine; at $4,100+ gold, the economics of Idaho sulphide underground systems are materially stronger than the price assumptions in Beartrack's 2023 pre-feasibility study, making each new drill result incrementally more significant for the project's ultimate production case.

headline: NEVADA GOLD MINES (BARRICK-NEWMONT JV) PAYS C$32.7M FOR RIDGELINE'S 4 NEVADA GOLD PROJECTS — 350%+ Return On Capital; Deal Price Exceeds Ridgeline's Entire Market Cap (TSX-V: RDG)
snippet: Ridgeline Minerals Corp. (TSX-V: RDG) completed the sale of its Swift, Black Ridge, Bell Creek, and Atlas gold exploration projects in Nevada's Carlin and Cortez Trends to Nevada Gold Mines LLC — the Barrick-Newmont joint venture — for US$23.15 million all-cash (C$32.7 million), effective August 3, 2026. The price represented a 26% premium to Ridgeline's 20-day VWAP, exceeded the company's entire pre-announcement market capitalisation, and delivered a return on invested capital across the four projects exceeding 350% — a textbook demonstration of the junior exploration value creation model in Nevada's prolific Carlin-Cortez corridor, where a major mine operator systematically pays significant premiums for adjacent early-stage ground that adds optionality to existing billion-ounce mine complexes.

headline: ROCKY SHORE GOLD DISCOVERS LUCKY 13 ZONE — 15.0m @ 2.04 g/t Au, 1,800m Strike, Open In All Directions; Grades Increasing At Depth In Newfoundland (CSE: RSG)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Rocky Shore Gold
snippet: Rocky Shore Gold Ltd. (CSE: RSG) announced the discovery of a new named zone — the Lucky 13 Gold Zone — at the Lane Pond Gold Target within its 100%-owned Gold Anchor Project in central Newfoundland, the second-largest property (over 1,200 km²) in an emerging Canadian gold belt. Twenty-five diamond drill holes (8,086 metres) have been completed with 15 holes assayed, confirming Lucky 13 across 1,800 metres of strike and more than 500 metres of dip extent, running 6.38 to 17.02 metres thick — with gold grades increasing at depth in a pattern consistent with a system widening and strengthening toward plunge, not pinching out. The highlight intersection of 15.0 metres at 2.04 g/t Au including 5.0 metres at 3.85 g/t Au fits the scale template of Newfoundland discoveries that have attracted senior gold producer interest in a province that has been outpacing exploration investment relative to its geological potential.

headline: GALWAY METALS DRILLS 48.0m @ 2.6 g/t AU AT CLARENCE STREAM SOUTHWEST — 14 Holes Confirm Broad Zone Continuity; 2.7Moz Resource Advancing To PEA (TSX-V: GWM)
snippet: Galway Metals Inc. (TSX-V: GWM; OTCQB: GAYMF) reported results from 14 diamond drill holes at the Southwest Deposit within its 100%-owned Clarence Stream Gold Project in New Brunswick, with highlights of 48.0 metres at 2.6 g/t gold and multiple higher-grade internal intervals, confirming broad mineralisation continuity across one of the project's most important deposits. The results add to an existing Mineral Resource Estimate of 27.2 million tonnes at 1.62 g/t for 1.42 million ounces Indicated and 28.5 million tonnes at 1.40 g/t for 1.29 million ounces Inferred (2.7 million ounces total), which is now being advanced to a Preliminary Economic Assessment — a de-risking step whose economics at $4,100+ gold are materially more attractive than when the resource was last evaluated at lower price assumptions.

headline: ORETERRA STARTS FIRST-EVER DRILL AT TREK SOUTH PORPHYRY — Glacial Retreat Revealed Never-Drilled Cu-Au Target Adjacent To Galore Creek JV, Golden Triangle BC (TSX-V: OTMC)
snippet: Oreterra Metals Corp. (TSX-V: OTMC) commenced a maiden 10,000-metre drill program at the Trek South porphyry copper-gold prospect in BC's Golden Triangle, directly adjacent to Teck-Newmont's Galore Creek copper-gold porphyry complex — a target that was entirely inaccessible until a dramatic recent glacial ice retreat exposed mineralized surface for the first time. The fully funded program (C$9.7 million financing closed) deploys two drills from an on-site camp located 1.2 km from the partially constructed Galore Creek road, with initial results anticipated in August 2026. Trek South represents a high-priority first-mover opportunity: never-drilled ground in a proven porphyry corridor, with infrastructure access under active construction and decades of Galore Creek drilling validating the geological setting directly alongside the prospect.

headline: KAZATOMPROM H1 2026 URANIUM OUTPUT SURGES 9% TO 13,291 TONNES — Realized Price Up 16% To $67.88/lb; Sales Volume Slips As Term Market Tightens
snippet: Kazatomprom — the world's largest uranium producer — reported August 3 that Kazakhstan's first-half 2026 uranium output rose 9% year-on-year to 13,291 tonnes (attributable basis: up 10% to 7,054 tonnes), while the average realised price of uranium concentrate jumped 16% to US$67.88 per pound. However, total uranium sales declined 1% to 7,586 tonnes — a divergence that implies Kazatomprom is directing more material into long-term contracts and away from spot, consistent with the term market reaching 18-year highs above $90/lb. The combination of rising output, rising realised prices, and falling spot sales is structurally bullish for uranium developers: the world's swing producer is generating record revenue while exercising volume discipline that keeps the spot price elevated, providing a stronger floor for the project economics of producers like Boss Energy and NexGen than simple supply volume would suggest.

headline: CANADA CRITICAL MINERALS ACCELERATOR LAUNCHES — First Phosphate Gets $4.8M For Begin-Lamarche Phosphate-Battery Mine Infrastructure In Saguenay (CSE: PHOS)
snippet: Natural Resources Canada announced August 5 in Saguenay the first agreement under its newly launched Canada Critical Minerals Accelerator — a nearly $5 million investment under the First and Last Mile Fund to advance power transmission and transportation infrastructure linking First Phosphate Corp.'s (CSE: PHOS) Begin-Lamarche phosphate mine in Quebec's Saguenay-Lac-Saint-Jean region to regional rail networks and the Port of Saguenay. The funding, which covers feasibility and environmental studies and Indigenous engagement, follows Canada formally adding phosphate to its Critical Minerals List — making Begin-Lamarche eligible for the full federal support suite previously reserved for lithium, cobalt, and nickel. The Accelerator is designed to bridge the 'first and last mile' infrastructure gap that kills otherwise viable critical mineral projects in remote Canadian jurisdictions, and investors should track which projects secure early agreements as early indicators of commercial development trajectories.

headline: GOLDSEEK GOLD SWOT: EVOLUTION MINING BUYS CARNABY'S COPPER GROWTH PIPELINE — Sector Dividends Hit $10.9B YTD Record; Miners Pivoting Capital To Critical Metals
snippet: US Global Investors' August 3 Gold SWOT analysis highlights Evolution Mining's A$213 million acquisition of Carnaby Resources — adding 10,000 tonnes per annum of copper production potential adjacent to the Ernest Henry copper-gold operation in Queensland — as the clearest indicator yet that Australian senior gold producers are systematically reallocating free cash flow from gold margins into copper growth pipeline assets. The SWOT notes that annualised dividends and buybacks for senior gold producers globally have hit US$10.9 billion year-to-date in 2026, already surpassing 2025's full-year record of US$8.6 billion, indicating that free cash flow is now both large enough to fund consolidation and large enough to return capital simultaneously — the hallmark of a gold sector that has structurally re-rated and is now attracting generalist equity fund managers who have historically avoided the sector as a capital-destruction vehicle.
